name: SoMa / Market St / Happy Valley dunes
note: Dunes 80-89 ft high on Market St (2nd-3rd, at Grant Ave) cut down by steam paddy and dumped into Yerba Buena Cove and the Mission marshes; steam paddy filling 1852-1873 (Dow 1973 p.31; NRHP Embarcadero nomination). year_end = midpoint of levelling. Exact pre-colonial geometry for northern SF: data/raw/sfei_hidden_nature_sf/sf_historical_habitats_2021.geojson (SFEI 2021, field HabitatCla) - prefer it over this coarse ring.

name: Western Addition / Hayes Valley dunes (Van Ness to Divisadero)
note: Sand hills between the old city and Lone Mountain; graded as the Western Addition was laid out and built up 1860s-1880s (estimated; city limits reached Divisadero 1851). year_end estimated. Exact pre-colonial geometry for northern SF: data/raw/sfei_hidden_nature_sf/sf_historical_habitats_2021.geojson (SFEI 2021, field HabitatCla) - prefer it over this coarse ring.

name: Inner Richmond dunes (Arguello to Park Presidio)
note: 'Great Sand Waste' with cemeteries, ranches and dairies before 1900; streetcar suburb; building surged after the 1906 earthquake (refugee camp Richmond) - range c.1890-1915, year_end = midpoint (estimated).

name: Outer Richmond dunes (Park Presidio to the ocean)
note: Last dunes and coastal scrub built over after 1906 as a streetcar suburb; range c.1906-1945 (estimated midpoint).

name: Golden Gate Park east of Strawberry Hill (incl. Panhandle)
note: Park Act 1870; dune reclamation began 1871 at the east end; 22,000 trees set out 1872, ~60,000 by 1875 (data/tables/parks.csv, NRHP 04001137). Cover after = park woods (viewer ground layer).

name: Golden Gate Park west of Strawberry Hill
note: ~600 acres west of Strawberry Hill forested later; west end finished c.1900 (Beach Chalet 1900, windmills 1902-08) (parks.csv / NRHP).

name: Inner Sunset dunes (Stanyan to 19th Ave)
note: In the early 1900s most of the Sunset was windswept dunes; Inner Sunset built first (streetcar on Lincoln Way laid among tall dunes Jan 1906; N-Judah 1928). Range c.1900-1930, estimated.

name: Outer Sunset dunes (19th Ave to Ocean Beach)
note: Built over 1920s-1950s by tract builders (e.g. Doelger); 'by the mid-1900s almost all had been developed' (Ungaretti, FoundSF). SFEI mobile-dune inland edge mapped for 1852 and 1873 (data/raw/sfei_hidden_nature_sf/mobile_dune_sheet_boundary_featurecollection.json). Range c.1925-1955, estimated midpoint.

name: Parkside / Lakeshore / Stonestown dunes
note: Dunes and sand hills north and east of Lake Merced, developed 1920s-1950s (Parkmerced on Spring Valley land bought by Metropolitan Life in 1940). Estimated.

name: Fort Funston / Lake Merced west dunes (still dunes)
note: Coastal dunes and bluffs west of Lake Merced remain open sand/scrub today (military reservation, now GGNRA). Exact pre-colonial geometry for northern SF: data/raw/sfei_hidden_nature_sf/sf_historical_habitats_2021.geojson (SFEI 2021, field HabitatCla) - prefer it over this coarse ring.

name: Presidio coastal scrub / grassland / dunes
note: Treeless scrub, grass and sand until the Army's mass planting from Arbor Day 1886 under Maj. W.A. Jones's 1883 plan; 329,975 trees by 1892 (parks.csv). Lobos Creek dunes partly restored since the 1990s.

name: Twin Peaks / Mt Sutro / Mt Davidson / Diamond Heights hills
note: Grassland and coastal scrub on the central hills; Sutro planted eucalyptus on Mt Sutro/Mt Davidson from 1886 (Arbor Day); Twin Peaks summits kept as grass/scrub (park 1915); slopes (Diamond Heights, Midtown Terrace) built 1950s-60s. year_end = typical development of the slopes; keep summits (park polygons) as scrub to 9999. Exact pre-colonial geometry for northern SF: data/raw/sfei_hidden_nature_sf/sf_historical_habitats_2021.geojson (SFEI 2021, field HabitatCla) - prefer it over this coarse ring.

name: Potrero Hill / Bernal Heights / Bayview hills grassland
note: Grassy hills used as pasture ('potrero' = pasture, Rancho Rincon de las Salinas y Potrero Viejo) until urbanised in the later 19th century (Dow p.99). year_end estimated; Bernal and Bayview hilltops later. Exact pre-colonial geometry for northern SF: data/raw/sfei_hidden_nature_sf/sf_historical_habitats_2021.geojson (SFEI 2021, field HabitatCla) - prefer it over this coarse ring.

name: Mission valley oak woodland, willow groves and Laguna de los Dolores
note: Sheltered Mission valley: coast live oak woodland, willow groves, wet meadow and the Laguna de los Dolores (SFEI Hidden Nature SF maps ~1,280 acres of oak woodland in northern SF). Mission San Francisco de Asis founded 1776 (Dow p.82). Exact pre-colonial geometry for northern SF: data/raw/sfei_hidden_nature_sf/sf_historical_habitats_2021.geojson (SFEI 2021, field HabitatCla) - prefer it over this coarse ring.

name: Mission Dolores fields and pasture
note: Mission and early American gardens/pasture in the Mission valley until street grading and the steam paddy levelled it ('between Sixth and Mission Dolores', 1870 directory; Dow p.86). year_end estimated.

name: Oakland hills 'San Antonio' redwood forest
note: ~5 sq mi of old-growth redwood (trunks 12-20 ft) along the Oakland ridge; logged 1845-1860, 'by 1860 the entire forest had been obliterated'; ridge trees were navigation marks for ships (Wikipedia; Save the Redwoods). Ring approximate (Redwood Regional Park / Joaquin Miller / Montclair).

name: Oakland hills second-growth redwoods
note: Second-growth redwood regrew from stumps; now Redwood Regional Park (smaller than the original forest). Start year LOW confidence (trees regrow over decades).

name: East Bay hills grassland, oak woodland and chaparral
note: Hills above the flatlands stay grazed grassland with oak woodland in canyons and chaparral on ridges; Eucalyptus/Monterey pine plantations from the 1880s-1910s are not in this cover list. Use SFEI Alameda Creek / East Contra Costa historical ecology layers where they apply (data/raw/sfei_historical_ecology/).

name: Oakland / Alameda 'Encinal' oak woodland (flatlands)
note: Coast live oak groves on the Oakland plain and the Alameda peninsula ('Encinal' = oak grove); cleared as the towns grew after 1850. year_end estimated. Oakland's name refers to these oaks.

name: San Leandro / Hayward / Eden Township orchards and grain
note: Eden Township 'covered with orchards and grain fields'; San Leandro cherries (cherry festival 1909), Hayward apricots, prunes, cherries; 1940s-50s transformation to suburbs (City of San Leandro; Hayward Area Historical Society). Range LOW.

name: Central Contra Costa valleys (Walnut Creek / Concord / Clayton / Pleasant Hill)
note: Wheat was the county's leading crop for decades in the later 1800s, peaking in the 1880s and shipped from Port Costa (Contra Costa County Historical Society).

name: Central Contra Costa walnut / pear / apricot orchards
note: Apricots, pears, walnuts and vines; walnuts replaced vines after 1919 and peaked in 1946; Walnut Creek grew from 2,460 (1950) to 9,900 (1960) as orchards became large-lot suburbs (cocohistory.org; goldennugget library).

name: Livermore Valley vineyards
note: First vines 1846 (Robert Livermore); Cresta Blanca 1882, Wente and Concannon 1883; 5,500-6,000 acres by the 1890s; phylloxera in the 1890s and Prohibition (1920-33) halved the wineries (Wikipedia; LVWA). Ring = valley floor south of Livermore, approximate; dips not modelled.

name: Santa Clara Valley floor oak savanna ('Llano de los Robles')
note: Valley known as the Llano de los Robles (Plain of the Oaks) when Mission Santa Clara was founded 12 Jan 1777 (Santa Clara Univ.). Detailed pre-contact habitats: data/raw/sfei_historical_ecology/santa_clara_valley_{west,south}.geojson and coyote_creek.geojson (SFEI).

name: Santa Clara Valley mission & rancho cattle range
note: Mission and Mexican-era rancho cattle grazing on the valley grassland/oak savanna; American settlers from the early 1830s (City of Santa Clara). Cover 'dairy_pasture' used for open grazing land.

name: Santa Clara Valley wheat / grain era
note: Dry wheat farming dominated in the 1850s-60s; fruit gradually became the main crop in the 1870s (Wikipedia Santa Clara Valley).

name: Santa Clara Valley orchards ('Valley of Heart's Delight')
note: Prunes and apricots: 79,000 acres of orchards at the end of WWI, ~100,000 acres at the 1930s-40s peak; nation's largest prune exporter 1920-40; largest fruit-packing region until c.1960, then suburbs and electronics (SJSU; Wikipedia). Grow toward the 1930s-40s peak; urbanisation from the 1950s (use building years).

name: Woodside / Kings Mountain redwood forest
note: Water-powered sawmill 1849; at least 8 sawmills + a shingle mill in Woodside by 1855; five mills near Huddart Park 1852-60; mills moved up the canyons as the lower hills were cut, replaced by farms, ranches and vineyards; estates from the 1880s (Town of Woodside; NPS HRS). year_end = end of the main logging boom, approximate.

name: Peninsula second-growth redwoods (Huddart / Wunderlich / Purisima)
note: Second growth on the steeper Skyline slopes (now county/open-space parks). Start year LOW confidence.

name: Point Reyes peninsula coastal scrub / grassland (pre-dairy)
note: Coastal prairie and scrub grazed by Mexican-era cattle before the Shafter era.

name: Point Reyes dairy ranches
note: James and Oscar Shafter took control in 1857; Charles Howard partner 1865; 31-33 lettered tenant dairies; by the 1870s Marin led California in butter and cheese; Point Reyes National Seashore 1962, several historic dairies still operating (NPS).

name: Muir Woods old-growth redwoods (never logged)
note: Old-growth coast redwood in Redwood Canyon on Mt Tamalpais; protected as a National Monument in 1908.

name: Napa Valley floor oak savanna / grassland
note: Valley oak savanna, grassland and wet meadows; detailed: data/raw/sfei_historical_ecology/napa_valley.geojson (SFEI Napa Valley Historical Ecology Atlas). year_end = start of rancho/American farming, approximate.

name: Napa Valley vineyards (first boom)
note: Commercial vineyards from the 1860s; phylloxera destroyed >90% of Napa vineyards 1889-1900, plantings ~2,000 acres by 1900 (Napa Valley Vintners; Wikipedia).

name: Napa Valley prunes / walnuts / pasture during the phylloxera & Prohibition years
note: After phylloxera and during Prohibition (1920-33) much of the valley floor was in other crops; only about a dozen wineries survived Prohibition; growth picked up mid-century and vineyard acreage regained its old level by the mid-1970s (Wikipedia; NVV). Crop mix LOW confidence - treat as mixed farmland/orchard.

name: Napa Valley vineyards (modern)
note: Replanting from the 1960s; 1976 Judgment of Paris; valley floor now nearly all vineyard (Wikipedia).

name: Sonoma Valley vineyards and orchards
note: Same arc as Napa (1860s planting, 1890s phylloxera, 1920-33 Prohibition, post-1970 revival); dips not modelled. LOW confidence on Sonoma-specific dates (no Sonoma acreage source found).

name: South Bay salt evaporation ponds
note: Ponds grow 1853-1957 (see fill_zones sb_salt_ponds_*); restored ponds return to marsh/water from 2006 (see restored zones). Clip to historical marsh/flat; TIGER maps the ponds as land.

name: Napa River salt ponds
note: ~10,000 acres created by Leslie Salt in the 1950s on diked hay land; restoration breaches from 2006-08 (CDFW).

name: Diked North Bay baylands in hay and dairy pasture
note: Diked marsh in oat hay and grazing from the early American period (see fill_zones nb_*_diked); parts become salt ponds 1950s and tidal marsh again after 2006-2015 restorations.
